column3: “the statute of the law” renders “the statute of the torah (instruction)” (also “law” in verse 14).
NASB uses passives, “it shall be brought … and be slaughtered,” for the Hebrew “he shall bring it … and one shall slaughter it.”
“water to remove impurity” renders “water of niddah (impurity)” (also in verses 13 and 20–21), and “purification from sin” renders “a sin offering (hatta’t).”
“the corpse of any person” renders “the dead body of any soul (nefesh) of man.”
“purify himself from uncleanness” renders “cleanse himself from sin” (also in verses 13 and 20), and “with the water” renders “with it.”
“no covering tied down on it” renders “no cover of cord on it.”
“the open field” renders “the face of the field,” and “who has died naturally” renders “a dead body.”
“the ashes” renders “the dust,” “the burnt purification from sin” renders “the burning of the sin offering,” and “flowing water” renders “living water.”
“the furnishings” renders “the vessels,” and “the one dying naturally” renders “the dead body.”
“he shall purify him from uncleanness” renders “he shall cleanse him from sin.”
